In [[mathematics]], a '''Somos sequence''' is a sequence of numbers defined by a certain [[recurrence relation]], described below.  They were discovered by mathematician [[Michael Somos]]. From the form of their defining recurrence (which involves division), one would expect the terms of the sequence to be fractions, but surprisingly, a few Somos sequences have the property that all of their members are integers.

==Recurrence equations==
For an integer number <math>k</math> larger than <math>1</math>, a Somos-<math>k</math> sequence <math>\{a_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}</math> is a solution of the equation
<math display=block>a_n a_{n-k} = \sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor} \alpha_i a_{n-i} a_{n-k+i}</math>
where <math>\alpha_1</math>, <math>\alpha_2</math>, ..., <math>\alpha_{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor}</math> are fixed parameters.
It can be rearranged into the form of an order <math>k</math> [[recurrence relation]]
<math display=block>a_n = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor} \alpha_i a_{n-i} a_{n-k+i}}{a_{n-k}}.</math> 
Hence a non-degenerate solution is determined by a choice of <math>k</math> initial values <math>a_0</math>, <math>a_1</math>, ..., <math>a_{k - 1}</math>. The sequence yielded by setting <math>\alpha_1 = \alpha_2 = \dots = \alpha_{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor} = 1</math> and <math>a_0 = a_1 = \dots = a_{k - 1} = 1</math> is referred to as <em>the</em> Somos-<math>k</math> sequence. The Somos-<math>k</math> sequence is symmetric, i.e., <math>s_{-n} = s_{n + k - 1}</math>.

For <math>k = 2</math> or <math>3</math>, the defining relations are very simple (there is no addition on the right-hand side).

In the first nontrivial case, <math>k = 4</math>, the relation is
<math display=block>a_n = \frac{\alpha a_{n-1} a_{n-3} + \beta a_{n-2}^2}{a_{n-4}}</math>
where <math>\alpha</math> and <math>\beta</math> are constant parameters.
In the case <math>k = 5</math> the relation is
<math display=block>a_n = \frac{\alpha a_{n-1} a_{n-4} + \beta a_{n-2} a_{n-3}}{a_{n-5}}.</math>

==Sequence values==
The Somos-<math>2</math> and Somos-<math>3</math> sequences are the all-ones sequences (..., <math>1</math>, <math>1</math>, <math>1</math>, <math>1</math>, <math>1</math>, ...).

The values in the Somos-<math>4</math> sequence are
:1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 7, 23, 59, 314, 1529, 8209, 83313, 620297, 7869898, ... {{OEIS|A006720}}.
The values in the Somos-<math>5</math> sequence are
:1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 11, 37, 83, 274, 1217, 6161, 22833, 165713, ... {{OEIS|A006721}}.
The values in the Somos-<math>6</math> sequence are
:1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 5, 9, 23, 75, 421, 1103, 5047, 41783, 281527, ... {{OEIS|A006722}}.
The values in the Somos-<math>7</math> sequence are
:1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 5, 9, 17, 41, 137, 769, 1925, 7203, 34081, ... {{OEIS|A006723}}.
The first 17 values in the Somos-<math>8</math> sequence are
:1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 7, 13, 25, 61, 187, 775, 5827, 14815 [the next value is fractional].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Mase | first = Takafumi
 | contribution = The Laurent phenomenon and discrete integrable systems
 | contribution-url = https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~kenkyubu/bessatsu/open/B41/pdf/B41_003.pdf
 | mr = 3220414
 | pages = 43–64
 | publisher = Res. Inst. Math. Sci. (RIMS), Kyoto
 | series = RIMS Kôkyûroku Bessatsu
 | title = The breadth and depth of nonlinear discrete integrable systems
 | volume = B41
 | year = 2013}}</ref>

==Integrality and the Laurent phenomenon==
The form of the recurrences describing the Somos sequences involves divisions, making it appear likely that the sequences defined by these recurrence will contain fractional values. Nevertheless, for <math>k \le 7</math> the Somos sequences contain only integer values.<ref>{{citation |last=Malouf |first=Janice L. |title=An integer sequence from a rational recursion |journal=[[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]] |volume=110 |number=1–3 |pages=257–261 |year=1992 |doi=10.1016/0012-365X(92)90714-Q |doi-access=free}}.</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref>{{citation |title=A Bare-Bones Chronology of Somos Sequences |url=https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/somos/chronology.html |access-date=2023-11-27 |website=faculty.uml.edu}}</ref>
Generally, for <math>k \le 7</math>, a Somos-<math>k</math> sequence satisfies the so-called Laurent property. That is, as a function of the initial terms <math>a_0</math>, ..., <math>a_{k-1}</math>, every term <math>a_n</math> is a multivariate [[Laurent polynomial]] with coefficients in <math>\mathbb{Z}[\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor}]</math>. 
Several mathematicians have studied the problem of proving and explaining this property of the Somos sequences; it is closely related to the combinatorics of [[cluster algebra]]s.<ref>{{citation | first1=Sergey | last1=Fomin | author-link1=Sergey Fomin | first2=Andrei | last2=Zelevinsky | author-link2=Andrei Zelevinsky | title=The Laurent phenomenon | journal=[[Advances in Applied Mathematics]]| volume=28 | year=2002 | issue=2 | pages=119&ndash;144 | doi=10.1006/aama.2001.0770 | arxiv=math.CO/0104241 | s2cid=119157629 }}.</ref><ref name=":0">{{citation | first1=Gabriel D. | last1=Carroll | first2=David E. | last2=Speyer | journal=[[Electronic Journal of Combinatorics]] | volume=11 | year=2004 | article-number= R73 | title=The Cube Recurrence| doi=10.37236/1826 | arxiv=math.CO/0403417 | s2cid=1446749 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Hone | first = Andrew N. W.
 | arxiv = 2111.10905
 | doi = 10.1017/S0017089522000167
 | issue = S1
 | journal = [[Glasgow Mathematical Journal]]
 | mr = 4594276
 | pages = S87–S101
 | title = Casting light on shadow Somos sequences
 | volume = 65
 | year = 2023}}</ref><ref>{{citation |last=Stone |first=Alex |date=18 November 2023 |title=The Astonishing Behavior of Recursive Sequences |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/the-astonishing-behavior-of-recursive-sequences-20231116/ |magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]}}</ref>

For <math>k \ge 8</math> the Somos-<math>k</math> sequences eventually contain fractional values. For Somos-<math>8</math> the first fractional value is the 18th term with value <math>420514/7</math>.

==Closed formula==
Consider a Somos-<math>4</math> relation
<math display=block>a_n a_{n-4} = \alpha a_{n-1} a_{n-3} + \beta a_{n-2}^2</math>
with <math>\alpha \ne 0</math>.
Then a [[Complex number|complex]]-valued Somos-<math>4</math> sequence corresponds to an [[arithmetic sequence]] of points <math>Q + n P</math> on an [[elliptic curve]] <math>E</math> (see [[Elliptic curve#Group law]]).
The general term is given by the formula<ref>{{citation
 | last = Hone | first = Andrew N. W.
 | doi = 10.1112/S0024609304004163
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Bulletin of the [[London Mathematical Society]]
 | pages = 161-171
 | title = Elliptic Curves and Quadratic Recurrence Sequences
 | volume = 37
 | year = 2005}}</ref>
<math display=block>a_n = A B^n \frac{\sigma(z_0 + n \kappa)}{\sigma(\kappa)^{n^2}}</math>
where <math>\sigma(z) = \sigma(z; g_2, g_3)</math> denotes the [[Weierstrass sigma function]] associated with the curve <math>E</math> written in the [[Weierstrass normal form|canonical form]]
<math display=block>E: \quad y^2 = 4 x^3 - g_2 x - g_3.</math>
The six parameters <math>g_2, g_3, A, B, z_0, \kappa \in \mathbb{C}</math> are determined uniquely (up to a choice of sign) by the coefficients <math>\alpha, \beta</math> and the initial terms <math>a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3</math>. The <math>(x, y)</math> coordinates of the sequence <math>Q + n P</math> are given by <math>(\wp(z_0 + n \kappa), \wp'(z_0 + n \kappa))</math>, where <math>\wp(z) = \wp(z; g_2, g_3)</math> denotes the [[Weierstrass elliptic function]].
The coefficients <math>\alpha</math> and <math>\beta</math> are given as [[elliptic functions]] of <math>\kappa</math> by
<math display=block>\alpha = \wp(\kappa)^2, \quad \beta =\wp'(\kappa)^2 (\wp(2 \kappa) - \wp(\kappa)).</math>
